angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 166,968 km at 96.32 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.3822 +/- 0.0362 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 96.32 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.24 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Muirhead et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-446 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...801...18M/abstract): 166,968 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.22 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Muirhead et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-446 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...801...18M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3359 +/- 60 K from Muirhead et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-446 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...801...18M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Muirhead et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-446 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...801...18M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-446.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.020, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
